deviations.what: Extend t7's file scope to include tests/test_discord_integration.py, and let the main agent apply the one-line fix at the merge gate rather than sending the task agent back.
deviations.reason: t7's confirmed scope (user.py + test_discord_user.py) omitted tests/test_discord_integration.py, whose line 45 asserts the OLD single-object 'user get --json' shape. The approved always-array breaking change (c17, q1) necessarily invalidates that assertion, and no task in the plan owns that file — so the plan as confirmed could not reach a green suite for wave 1. A scoping error in the plan, not a failure by the task agent, which correctly refused to widen its own allowlist and reported the breakage.

deviations.what: t9's acceptance criterion 1 cannot be met as written: the 413 CliError surfaces Discord's own status text instead of 'naming the byte size that was sent'.
deviations.reason: discord.py 2.7.1's HTTPException.__init__ records only response, status, code and text — the outgoing request's byte size is never captured, and neither the exception nor the aiohttp response it wraps exposes it. Verified directly against the installed source, independently of the task agent's report. Since the q2 decision forbids a size pre-flight, no earlier layer recorded the size either, so at discord_client.run's handler chain the number is genuinely unrecoverable. The task brief pre-authorised this fallback ('do not fabricate a size'), and the agent took it rather than inventing a plausible number.

deltas.behavior_text: channel messages reports stopped_by='limit' when the collected count lands EXACTLY on --limit, even if the window happened to end there. The API cannot distinguish the two, so the pessimistic reading was chosen: a spurious 'come back for more' over a false 'you have everything'. The plan did not specify this boundary case.

--since accepts a duration suffix 'm' meaning MONTHS, approximated as 30 days (units h/d/w/m). The plan left the unit set open; months was chosen over minutes and the approximation is documented in the module docstring and named in the error hint.

--since REJECTS a bare naive timestamp such as '2026-06-01T12:00:00' as ambiguous rather than assuming a timezone. The plan named three accepted forms but did not say what happens to a fourth; refusing is the honest choice given discord.py reads a naive datetime as local time.

channel messages emits a stderr diagnostic in text mode when --limit cut a windowed walk short. The plan specified the --json coverage signal only; text-mode users would otherwise get a silently truncated read with no signal at all.

The live lane gained a DISCORD_TEST_PAGING_SINCE env var, and its paging test calls pytest.fail (not skip) when the window holds <= 100 messages. The plan asked for a paging test but did not specify how to prevent it passing vacuously on a thin channel.
